title: Keep the power bank awake
story: A USB power bank switches itself off when less than 20 mA is drawn from its 5 V output. Your gadget sleeps most of the time and draws almost nothing, so you add a 'keep-alive' resistor across the output. You only have 1/4 W resistors, and they will sit in a warm, closed case, so you decide each one may dissipate at most 0.15 W. Pick the resistor.

goals.label: at least 20 mA so the power bank stays on
resistor stays under 0.15 W (derated 1/4 W part)

hints: The full 5 V sits across the resistor, so I = 5 / R and P = 25 / R.
The current goal sets a MAXIMUM resistance: R must be at most 5 / 0.020 = 250 ohm.
The power goal sets a MINIMUM resistance: R must be at least 25 / 0.15 = about 167 ohm.
